page.description: Talos Linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An immutable Linux built only to run Kubernetes: no SSH, no shell and no package manager, with every change applied through an API and a machine configuration.
pros: Minimal, immutable image with nothing but the Kubernetes stack.
The whole node is managed by API and declarative machine config.
amd64 and arm64 metal images for ISO and raw-disk installs.
Upgrades are image swaps, so nodes are reproducible.
cons: No shell and no SSH: a broken config means reinstalling or fixing from outside.
The ISO installs to disk, erasing the target.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Talos Linux; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Boot the metal ISO and apply a machine configuration generated with talosctl; the node installs to the chosen disk and reboots into the installed system.

editions.name: Bare metal
editions.description: The metal ISO that boots and installs the node to disk, for amd64 and arm64 machines.
editions.usbNote: 347 MB (amd64) or 216 MB (arm64) image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.
